faq.title: A few things to know.
items: The current DMG targets Apple Silicon Macs with macOS 15 or later. Intel Macs, Windows and Linux are not supported by this release. It is a development preview; a clean Mac and macOS 15 have not yet been tested live.
Do I need an AI subscription?
No subscription is required by SaySpan. You can use a separately installed local Ollama model. Online services require your own credentials and may charge for API usage.
Does everything I type get sent to a model?

No. English direct typing does not request translation. During composition, the confirmed draft is sent to your chosen model after a short pause. Selection translation sends the selected text, not the surrounding document.
Can I type every supported translation language?

Translation offers a 16-language pair selector. Typing support differs: Chinese uses pinyin, Japanese uses romaji candidates, and several languages use native keyboard layouts. Korean translation is supported, but Korean syllable input is not available yet.
Where can I follow the project?
The public SaySpan repository is on GitHub. Check the repository for source availability, project updates and release announcements.

items.title: Getting started
items.summary: Install SaySpan, add the input source, and write your first sentence.
sections:
You need an Apple Silicon Mac running macOS 15 or later. The current release is a development preview, not Developer ID-signed or notarized. It has been checked on the development Mac; clean-machine installation and execution on macOS 15 remain unverified.

Translation needs a model: either a separately installed local Ollama model or your own OpenAI-compatible online service. Basic typing does not depend on successful translation.

1. Visit the SaySpan GitHub repository to check release availability. When a DMG is published there, download the compatible build. This website does not host installers.
  2. Finish any unfinished draft and switch to another input source before updating.
  3. Open the DMG and run Install SaySpan.pkg. Install it for the current user.

The app lives at ~/Library/Input Methods/SaySpan.app. It is not installed in the usual Applications folder. If macOS blocks it, review Apple’s guidance for opening apps safely. Only proceed if you trust this development build.
2. Add SaySpan to your input sources

1. Quit System Settings completely.
  2. Open Refresh Input Sources.command in the mounted DMG. It refreshes a generated input-source cache and opens Keyboard settings.
  3. Choose Keyboard → Text Input → Edit → + → Others → SaySpan → Add.
  4. Select SaySpan in the macOS input menu.

A first installation may require logging out and back in. The refresh helper backs up the cache; it does not change your enabled input sources, preferences or permissions.

With SaySpan selected, open the macOS input menu and choose Settings…. In Languages, choose First language and Second language. The defaults are English and Simplified Chinese.

In Models, choose a local Ollama model or configure your online provider. Save your changes. See Models & prompts for the full setup.

With the default English/Chinese pair, turn physical Caps Lock on to use Chinese. Type nihao, then press Space to confirm 你好. Press Enter to insert the original. Or wait for a translation and press Tab to insert it.

Turn Caps Lock off to type English directly. The active macOS input source remains SaySpan. Use Shift for uppercase letters.

items.title: Writing & keyboard controls
items.summary: Choose candidates, edit your sentence, and insert either language.
sections:
Chinese pinyin and Japanese romaji use a candidate list above the editable sentence. Space confirms the highlighted candidate. Number keys or a click select a visible numbered candidate.

While candidates are pending, all four arrow keys navigate them. Down or Page Down expands the list into multiple rows. Continue past an edge to move between pages. Page Up and Page Down jump pages once expanded.

Each row shows five candidates by default. Set 3–9 in Settings → Input. Long candidates wrap to fit the available space.

Once every pending candidate is confirmed, the arrows move the sentence caret. Up and Down move between visual lines. Hold Shift with an arrow to select part of the confirmed sentence.

Command+A, C, X, V and Z perform select-all, copy, cut, paste and undo inside the draft. Command+Shift+Z redoes. Delete and typing act on the selected section. Clearing the entire draft closes the panel; undo can restore it.

KeyWhat it does
SpaceConfirm the highlighted candidate; insert a space when no candidate is pending.
EnterWith pending spelling: keep the raw Latin letters in the draft. Otherwise: insert the original sentence.
TabInsert the ready translation after candidates have been confirmed. An early Tab does not queue a later insertion.
EscapeClear a selection, collapse expanded candidates, clear spelling or cancel the draft, depending on the current state.
Caps LockOff: first language. On: second language. During composition, insert the source sentence before switching.

Enter and Tab insertion do not send a Return to the host app or submit its form.

To keep an English word inside a Chinese sentence, type its letters and press Enter before choosing a candidate. The letters become part of your draft, without pinyin separators. A standalone Shift tap does the same while spelling is pending.

For example: hello → Enter → Space → shijie → Space creates hello 世界. Press Enter again to insert the draft, or Tab for its ready translation. Shift+letter inserts uppercase Latin text; punctuation follows the current language.

Under Settings → Input, candidate learning can prioritize Chinese and Japanese words and phrases you confirm. This vocabulary stays on your Mac and survives restarts. Turning learning off preserves it but uses the base ranking.

Confirming a candidate may teach the dictionary before the sentence is inserted. Canceling that draft does not undo an already learned conversion.

items.title: Selection translation
items.summary: Understand text in other apps without replacing the original.
sections:
Open Settings → Selection and enable selection translation. Then grant SaySpan access in System Settings → Privacy & Security → Accessibility.

If it is missing from the permission list, use the + button and navigate to ~/Library/Input Methods/SaySpan.app. In a file picker, Command+Shift+G lets you enter the folder path. This permission is only needed for reading selections in other apps; normal input does not need it.

Select text in a supported document or webpage. Click the small translation button beside the selection. The card stays at its initial position instead of following your mouse. The small copy icon at the top right copies the result.

Enable Automatic translation in the card or Settings to show the result after a selection settles, without clicking the button. This choice is saved immediately. Click outside to dismiss; reselect the text to retry.

SaySpan detects which of your two configured languages the selection uses and translates it into the other. Mixed text uses the dominant language. When detection is uncertain, selection translation targets the first language.

Selection translation pauses while you are composing in SaySpan, so the draft does not produce a second popup.

Line breaks, blank lines, indentation and list markers are preserved where the source app exposes them and the model’s output allows it. This is plain-text formatting, not font, color or rich-text styling.

The host must expose selected text through macOS Accessibility. Password fields and image OCR are not supported. Some Chromium-based apps take a few seconds to expose their contents. Selections over 6,000 UTF-16 code units are rejected before being sent to the model.

items.title: Models & translation prompts
items.summary: Set up local Ollama or connect your own compatible online API.
sections:
1. Install and open Ollama for macOS.
  2. Download a local model. For the app’s default model, run ollama pull qwen2.5:3b in Terminal.
  3. In SaySpan Settings → Models, choose Ollama, refresh the model list, select the downloaded model and Save.

The default local service is http://127.0.0.1:11434. Ollama and model weights are not included in the DMG. Model size, supported languages and speed vary with the model and hardware. See Ollama’s quickstart for service setup.

Select the OpenAI-compatible online provider. Enter your service’s API base URL, API key and text-chat model ID. Refresh the model list if supported, or enter the ID manually. The endpoint must support /chat/completions; discovery uses /models.

Use the base URL documented by your provider, not a full chat-completions URL. HTTPS is required except for explicit localhost services. Separate protocols such as Anthropic Messages are not implemented.

API keys are stored in macOS Keychain per endpoint. Leave the key field empty to keep an existing key for that endpoint. Online requests send the draft or selection to that provider and may incur charges. There is no silent fallback to another provider.

Start with Lowest (recommended). SaySpan maps recognized model families to their minimum supported setting. For an unknown model, it uses the service default.

If your provider rejects a reasoning parameter, choose Service default. Available levels depend on the provider and model; a higher setting is not a guarantee of better translation.

Under Settings → Prompt, edit the shared translation instructions in English or Chinese. They apply to both sentence and selection translation after saving.

Direction and formatting rules are added automatically. The default prompt asks the model to preserve details, negation, conditions and who performs each action, without extra explanations. You can restore the default and save. Always review important translations; model output can still be wrong.

items.title: Languages & switching
items.summary: Configure your language pair and understand available input engines.
sections:
In Settings → Languages, choose two different languages. Caps Lock off selects the first; on selects the second. The physical keyboard state is authoritative. Menu entries report the language and cannot switch it.

During composition, Caps Lock confirms the highlighted candidate, inserts the source sentence, then switches. There is no temporary language mode. Hold Shift to type uppercase English.

LanguageInput method
Simplified ChineseRime pinyin with candidate learning.
Traditional ChinesePinyin with OpenCC conversion; not Zhuyin or Cangjie.
JapaneseRime romaji with kana and kanji candidates. Phrase conversion, not the full Mozc engine.
English, IndonesianABC layout.
French, German, Spanish, Portuguese, ItalianThe corresponding macOS keyboard layout, including native accents.
Russian, Arabic, Hindi, Thai, VietnameseThe corresponding macOS keyboard layout. No alternate phonetic layouts yet.
KoreanTranslation supported; Hangul composition is not yet available. Current typing falls back to ABC.

English stays direct: ordinary English typing does not open the translation panel. Select English text afterward to translate it. The sentence candidate workflow is provided by the Chinese and Japanese engines.

The app’s interface supports English and Simplified Chinese. Settings → General → Interface language follows the system by default, with manual overrides. Save and reopen Settings to refresh its labels.

The website has its own language switch. It remembers your choice in this browser. Interface language does not change your input language pair.

items.title: Troubleshooting
items.summary: Missing input sources, model errors and selection permissions.
sections: SaySpan is missing or blank in Keyboard settings

Quit System Settings, then run Refresh Input Sources.command from the DMG. Reopen the input-source picker and look under Others. The helper backs up and refreshes a generated cache, without editing your enabled input-source list.

If it refuses to run, make sure System Settings is fully quit, not only its window closed. On a first installation, save your work and log out and back in if necessary.

The preview is not Developer ID-signed or notarized. Follow Apple’s instructions for safely opening software if you choose to trust it. A development preview is not a notarized public release. Do not disable Gatekeeper globally.
Typing works, but translation does not

Check the selected provider under Models. For Ollama, make sure the app is running and the chosen local model is installed; refresh the list. For online services, verify the base URL, model ID, API key, quota and provider-supported reasoning level.

Confirm pending candidates before pressing Tab. Tab only inserts a ready result; it does not schedule insertion for later. English direct typing intentionally does not request translations.

1. Check that selection translation is enabled in SaySpan Settings.
  2. Check SaySpan’s Accessibility permission. Updates to this development build may require renewed authorization.
  3. Make sure you have finished or canceled any input draft.
  4. Clear the old selection, then select text again and allow a few seconds for the host app.

The SaySpan process must be running. Some apps do not expose selected text. Image text and password fields are not supported. If the permission entry is stale, remove that app entry and add the current ~/Library/Input Methods/SaySpan.app again.

Before updating, finish your draft and switch to another input source. The installer replaces the app while preserving settings and learned vocabulary. Recheck Accessibility and Keychain access if macOS requests it.

To uninstall, switch to another input source, remove SaySpan from Keyboard settings, quit it, and move ~/Library/Input Methods/SaySpan.app to Trash. Ollama and its models are separate installations. This does not erase your saved settings or learned words.

items.title: Privacy & data
items.summary: Understand what stays on your Mac and what reaches a model.
sections:
During composition, SaySpan sends only the confirmed draft to your selected model after a short pause. Selection translation sends the selected text when you click the button or enable automatic display. It does not send the surrounding document.

With a locally running Ollama model, inference stays on the Mac. If you configure an online provider or remote endpoint, those requests leave your Mac and the provider’s terms and retention policies apply. SaySpan does not keep a translation history.

Language choices, model preferences and custom prompts are stored locally. Online API keys are stored in macOS Keychain per endpoint. Learned Chinese and Japanese vocabulary is stored on your Mac and is not synchronized or uploaded by SaySpan.

Selection translation needs macOS Accessibility permission. Ordinary composition uses InputMethodKit without Accessibility or clipboard injection. Selection reading does not use the clipboard; clicking Copy explicitly writes the result to it.

This website does not include advertising, analytics scripts, accounts or a live translation service. Its examples are prewritten. It saves only your website language preference in this browser’s local storage.

The hosting server and Cloudflare process normal request data such as IP addresses, requested URLs and user agents to deliver and protect the site. Downloading the app does not send your typed content to this website.
